definition: SAS (previously Statistical Analysis System) is a data and artificial intelligence software developed by SAS Institute for data management, advanced analytics, multivariate analysis, business intelligence, and predictive analytics.
details: SAS was developed at North Carolina State University from 1966 until 1976, when SAS Institute was incorporated. SAS was further developed in the 1980s and 1990s with the addition of new statistical procedures, additional components and the introduction of JMP. A point-and-click interface was added in version 9 in 2004. A social media analytics product was added in 2010. SAS Viya, a suite of analytics and artificial intelligence software, was introduced in 2016.

It was developed at North Carolina State University from 1966 until 1976, when SAS Institute was incorporated.

tiers.eli5: A long-established toolkit that businesses use to manage data and run statistical analyses.
tiers.practitioner: It was developed through the 1980s and 1990s with new statistical procedures, additional components, and JMP; a point-and-click interface arrived in version 9 in 2004, social media analytics in 2010, and the SAS Viya analytics and AI suite in 2016.
tiers.paperLevel: A commercial software platform spanning data management, analytics, and business intelligence rather than a single algorithm.

explainer.example: A business running predictive analytics and business intelligence on its data would use SAS Viya for the modern analytics and AI suite.
